automation_name: AI Dev Wiki Topic News Collector

cutoff_window.rule: Include only public sources with a visible publication or update date inside the last 2 days relative to the run time. Exclude missing, ambiguous, future-dated, or boundary-only dates.

federation_boundary.downstream_owned_lens: AI-assisted development practice: context architecture, guidance structure, agent operating practices, source workflows, verification, governance, and local adoption patterns.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot model routing adds parallel-tool coding-agent option
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub announced Gemini 3.6 Flash availability in GitHub Copilot, describing it as designed for web and app development, coding, longer-horizon agentic tasks, configurable reasoning effort, and parallel tool use.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local practice pages should treat model selection as a governed runtime-control question when agents can vary reasoning effort and invoke tools in parallel.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Record only the practice implication: configurable reasoning effort and parallel tool use require explicit model-routing, budget, and tool-permission policies rather than product encyclopedia coverage.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: During ingest, link to upstream model/product pages if needed and update local model-routing or tool-governance guidance only.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot cost centers gain UI-managed AI credit pools
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub added billing UI management for Copilot AI credit pools on cost centers, including automatic pool-limit calculation from assigned licenses and limit behavior that can block included usage or continue as overage spend.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI-assisted development operating models increasingly need spend governance that maps agent and assistant usage to teams, cost centers, and explicit overage decisions.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep the local lesson on budget boundaries, chargeback, and overage approval policy for AI-assisted development rather than duplicating GitHub billing documentation.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest target: adoption or governance leaf covering per-team AI spend controls.

qualifying_updates.title: Copilot users gain personal AI credit visibility
qualifying_updates.summary: GitHub added per-user visibility into Copilot AI credits used during the billing cycle, including users without an individual budget.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Personal usage visibility is a concrete adoption-control pattern: developers can see actual AI consumption rather than relying only on admin dashboards or percentage-of-budget abstractions.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local guidance can treat individual usage telemetry as part of responsible developer adoption, cost feedback loops, and agent-workload planning.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Consider folding into existing spend-governance or adoption telemetry pages during ingest.

qualifying_updates.title: CodeRabbit records full review history in Change Stack
qualifying_updates.summary: CodeRabbit added Change Stack visibility for full pull request review history, including human and bot approvals, comments, change requests, pending reviews, filtering, timeline sorting, and in-app review/comment viewing.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI code review workflows need auditable review timelines that include both human and bot states so teams can reconstruct approval paths and identify stale or conflicting review signals.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: The local practice lens is review-state provenance and auditability, not CodeRabbit product coverage.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: During ingest, compare with existing AI review gate and source workflow pages.

qualifying_updates.title: CodeRabbit exposes review rate-limit impact metrics
qualifying_updates.summary: CodeRabbit added billing usage metrics that show conditional rate-limit impact for users, limited reviews, review wait time, active users, and warnings when monthly spend approaches a configured cap.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Agentic review programs need operational signals for saturation, queues, spend caps, and review latency before teams rely on automated review as a delivery gate.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Track rate-limit and queue telemetry as first-class evidence when deciding whether AI review gates are reliable enough for normal delivery flow.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest target: review-capacity or runtime-telemetry leaf.

qualifying_updates.title: CodeRabbit automations manage incident webhooks through admin connection
qualifying_updates.summary: CodeRabbit added managed PagerDuty webhook subscriptions for Slack and workspace automations after a global admin connects PagerDuty from the automation editor, with selectable incident event types.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: When agent or review automations react to production incidents, connection ownership, webhook lifecycle management, and event-scope choices become governance controls.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture the local pattern as admin-owned connection setup plus scoped event triggers for incident-driven agent workflows.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Avoid duplicating PagerDuty or Slack background; keep only the workflow governance implication.

qualifying_updates.title: METR proposes expenditure horizon for agent optimization ability
qualifying_updates.summary: METR listed a new item titled "Expenditure Horizon: Measuring Optimization Ability, with an Application to NanoGPT," proposing a measure of an AI agent's optimization ability and applying it to a NanoGPT speedrun.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Software engineering eval pages can treat optimization over expenditure as a possible lens for long-horizon coding agents, especially when agents spend compute and attempts to improve a target artifact.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Keep the downstream note on eval design: measure agent improvement loops against expenditure and artifact outcomes, not only pass/fail task completion.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Fetch the article detail during ingest if a durable eval leaf needs exact definitions and methodology.

qualifying_updates.title: AI reviewer disagreement framed as a stop condition
qualifying_updates.summary: Contrast Security described a controlled multi-round AI code-review run where reviewers did not converge: after three rounds and about half an hour of agent time, the central security issue remained unresolved and the finding count grew.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: AI code-review loops need explicit non-convergence handling; additional rounds are not automatically evidence of progress when reviewers disagree about a fix.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Local review-loop guidance should add stop conditions for growing finding sets, unresolved central issues, and reviewer disagreement rather than trusting fixed round budgets.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: Potential ingest target: lifecycle AI review gates or verification-loop pages.

qualifying_updates.title: SonarQube Server release emphasizes AI-code verification gates
qualifying_updates.summary: Sonar announced SonarQube Server 2026.4 with a code verification layer for AI-generated code, architecture management, organization-wide quality-gate visibility, and an Agentic AI quality gate that prioritizes dependency security while tolerating minor style issues.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Teams adopting AI-generated code need quality gates that separate high-consequence security and dependency issues from lower-signal style findings, while also watching whether gates are bypassed.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Treat AI-code verification as a calibrated gate with security priority, architecture drift visibility, and bypass monitoring rather than a generic static-analysis update.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: During ingest, avoid a product leaf; fold the practice into verification gates and AI-generated-code review guidance.

qualifying_updates.title: Graph engineering post maps multi-agent topology to governance evidence
qualifying_updates.summary: TrueFoundry framed graph engineering as the design and operation of multi-agent systems as explicit graphs of agents, deterministic functions, routers, joins, tools, and human checkpoints, with emphasis on identities, graph/run/node identifiers, budgets, policy, traces, approvals, and orchestrator records.
qualifying_updates.why_it_matters: Local multi-agent guidance should distinguish topology governance from single-agent loop design and require correlation identifiers that connect orchestration traces with model, tool, policy, latency, and cost records.
qualifying_updates.local_practice_implication: Capture the downstream lens as topology-as-artifact, node identity, trace correlation, and approval checkpoint placement for multi-agent development workflows.
qualifying_updates.follow_up_notes: The term is emerging and contested; ingest should avoid treating it as a settled standard.
